The role: What's in the Box

As a Supply Risk Planner, you will support the day-to-day execution of supply risk tracking and operational planning across your assigned ingredient category. Sitting within the Supply Risk & Planning team and reporting  to the Associate Director of Supply Risk & Planning, you will drive routine risk analysis, monitor category metrics, and proactively evaluate emerging supply risks. You will act as a pragmatic problem solver and key operational liaison with Strategic Sourcing, SCO, Demand Planning, and Menu Planning across our EU markets.

What you’ll do: The Recipe

Long-Term Supply Risk & Planning (T-12 to T-52)

• Volume Commitments: Track supplier volume commitments for your category, identifying under- or over-committed volumes, and coordinate with Strategic Sourcing and Menu Planning to execute mitigation steps.

• Menu Planning Constraints: Maintain and update the catalogue of category supply constraints (e.g., SKU volume caps, supplier lead-time limits, minimum recipe frequency requirements) that feed into Menu Planning cycles.

• SKU Portfolio Reviews: Provide accurate data and category analysis for quarterly SKU portfolio reviews, ensuring active SKUs align with business performance and customer requirements.

Mid-Term Supply Risk & Planning (T-0 to T-12 - Menu Planned, Not Yet Live)

• Supply Volume Tracking: Monitor SKU and supplier-level forecast shifts in your category to identify emerging availability risks that require immediate mitigation.

• SKU Risk Database: Maintain the category SKU risk database and follow established risk management protocols. Partner with Strategic Sourcing, SCO, and FSQA to maintain updated risk scores per SKU and engage Menu Planning when demand steering is needed.

title: Director of Brand and Communications
description:
ABOUT HIYA

At Hiya, we’re making business calls more trusted, useful, and effective.

Voice remains one of the most important ways businesses communicate with their customers, but the value of a call depends on trust. When customers do not recognize who is calling or why, important conversations are missed, customer relationships suffer, and business outcomes are harder to achieve.

Hiya helps businesses create trusted calling experiences that benefit both sides of the conversation: enterprises can reach customers with confidence, and customers can answer with confidence. Our products support branded business calling, trusted caller identity, call performance insights, customer engagement, and voice security capabilities that help businesses strengthen relationships and improve outcomes.

This role sits in a core business area for Hiya and is focused on helping SMB and enterprise customers succeed.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This year we rewrote our story from the ground up - who we are, why we matter, and where we're going. Now we need someone to take that story global and make Hiya the voice the world trusts on the future of the phone call.

This is the role where it all comes together. You'll own how the world sees Hiya: the press, the analysts, the stages, our social channels, and the creative that ties it into one unmistakable brand. And it's a story with real range. The same Hiya has to land with a network executive in Madrid deciding how to protect millions of subscribers from AI scams, a sales leader in Toronto whose team's calls keep going unanswered, and a mom in Ohio who just got a deepfake call pretending to be her son asking for money.

You'll lead our existing creative + events teams and PR agencies, you'll build, and you'll get your hands dirty. Organic social doesn't exist here yet. You'll write the strategy, find our voice, and ship the first posts yourself. This is a director role for someone who still loves doing the work.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own the brand. Take the new narrative from slides to everywhere Hiya shows up, and set the visual and verbal identity so every touchpoint looks and sounds like one Hiya. Give teams what they need to stay on brand without asking permission.

- Flex the story without breaking it. Work with product marketing to tell it right for each audience, then make it land in each country, with its own pains and language.

- Set global PR strategy. Decide where we invest market by market, including how PR helps us break into new ones. Lead our agencies and keep the narrative owned in-house.

- Turn our data into headlines. Make our annual State of the Call report the one reporters, analysts, and operators wait for, and keep a steady drumbeat of data stories by market.

- Build analyst relations. Get Hiya in front of the analysts who shape how operators and businesses buy, and make sure they know our story cold.

- Build organic social as a function, not just a channel. Grow our executives' voices, set guardrails with legal so the team can move fast, create ideas that travel across paid, owned, earned, and AI search, and turn what we hear into intel for product, sales, and PR.

- Make Hiya a visible industry leader. Build the thought leadership and speaking program, prep spokespeople, and go after the keynotes and awards that put us at the center of voice security and AI fraud. Have a plan ready for when something goes sideways.

- Make events count. With our global events manager, set the event strategy: which events matter for which audiences, how we show up, and how we measure presence and relationships, not just leads. Flagship moments like Mobile World Congress should feel unmistakably Hiya.

- Build and lead the team. Coach and grow the team, run our agencies, and build a creative function that scales globally. Hire for where we're going.

- Measure what matters: share of voice, coverage quality, analyst perception, and how brand, PR, and social move people from awareness to consideration.

The Senior Director, GTM Revenue Operations, is both the strategic and technical backbone of how ChowNow's Sales, Onboarding, and Customer Success teams operate day to day. This is not a reporting-and-dashboards role - it's an operator and systems-architect role. You'll need to understand the GTM motion deeply enough to sit in a rep's or post sales rep's shoes, spot exactly where a process is broken or a workflow is creating friction, and then personally architect the fix - not as an isolated patch, but as part of a coherent system that holds up as we scale.

Small changes take too long, and they too often break something else in the process. We need someone who can see the whole board - not just the piece in front of them - untangle what's been glued together, and rebuild it so that future changes are fast, safe, and durable.
You'll lead three key functions: a Sales & CS Business Ops (who lives inside the sales and CS org, diagnosing friction and defining the fix), a Marketing & Partner Ops Manager (who owns the demand and partner tech stack end to end as our HubSpot admin), and a Biz Systems team who build and maintain our core systems. Your job is to make sure these three functions work as one connected system rather than three disconnected ones - translating GTM needs into technical requirements, and technical constraints back into GTM strategy, so nothing gets lost in either direction.
This role reports directly to the CEO and will own a team of 5-7 direct reports.
This is a remote role based in the United States. Please note: ChowNow is not eligible to employ in every state and the recruiting team will confirm location and eligibility before moving past initial stages.

title: Senior Backend Engineer
description:
Senior Backend Engineer
About us
We're creating the foundational backend systems that power private market access, from secure authentication and transaction processing to portfolio management and regulatory compliance.
The Role
We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to own the systems where money moves and balances have to be correct - the ledger, transaction processing, and the settlement and reconciliation workflows behind our platform. This is the correctness core of what we build. If a balance is wrong, a transaction double-processes, or a reconciliation silently drifts, nothing else we build matters.
You'll design the double-entry ledger, the money-movement engine, and the long-running state machines that carry complex financial workflows to completion reliably over hours, days, or weeks. You'll reason about idempotency, concurrency, partial failure, and replay as a matter of habit, not as an afterthought.
You'll own core infrastructure decisions and set the standard for how we build financial systems.
Requirements
What You'll Do

• Design and build the double-entry ledger and money-movement engine that all transactions reconcile against

• Model complex financial workflows as robust, observable state machines that run reliably over long periods

• Guarantee financial correctness under concurrency: idempotent operations, transactional integrity, and reconciliation that ties out to the cent

• Handle partial-failure and replay cases so no event is lost, duplicated, or applied twice

• Build secure, well-versioned APIs

• Design and optimize PostgreSQL schemas and data models

• Debug production issues and own the reliability of mission-critical financial workflows

What We're Looking For

• 5+ years of backend development on production systems

• Demonstrated money-movement correctness experience: you've built a ledger, settlement system, payments core, or transaction-processing system and can talk in detail about how you kept it correct

• Concurrency and idempotency depth: you can explain, from experience, how you handled double-processing, race conditions on balances, and replay

• Reconciliation experience: you've built or owned systems that had to tie out exactly, and you know what happens when they don't

• Strong TDD practices: you write tests first and maintain comprehensive coverage

• Domain-Driven Design expertise: you model complex financial domains accurately

• Deep PostgreSQL knowledge: schema design, transactions, isolation levels, optimization

• Strong in a modern backend stack: we work in TypeScript/Node.js, Go and on the JVM ecosystem; we value real depth in either and the range to pick up the other

• Cloud deployment experience

• Startup mentality: comfortable with ambiguity, high autonomy, driving solutions without detailed specs

Nice to Have

• Payments, banking, brokerage, or investment-platform systems experience

• Securities, custody, or portfolio/NAV domain knowledge

• Event-driven architectures and message queues

• Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, CloudFormation)

• Understanding of KYC/AML or compliance frameworks

• Accounting principles or financial modeling
